facts.text: Post Mountain’s roots trace back to the Wintu tribe, who called the area Nor Rel Muk Wintu Nation long before Euro-American fur trappers arrived.
The community sits in a high fire‑hazard zone, where historic suppression and climate change have spiked wildfire frequency and intensity.
Perched at 3,264 feet, Post Mountain lies along State Route 36, about 15 miles southwest of Hayfork and nine miles northeast of Forest Glen.
In the 1970s counterculture settlers began cultivating cannabis here, cementing Post Mountain’s place in the Emerald Triangle’s famed marijuana industry.
Soils range from sandstone and schist to serpentine, the latter’s magnesium and heavy metals limiting agriculture but supporting resilient native flora.
Post Mountain enjoys a Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers, cool, wet winters, with about 42 inches of rain mostly falling between October and April.
